description.value: Thunderbird is a Korean Fried Chicken restaurant tucked into Cook Street Village, one of Victoria's most bike-friendly neighbourhood strips. Founded by Korean-Canadians who moved to Victoria in 2009 and found no KFC restaurants in the city, it specialises in double deep-fried chicken with sauces like Yang-nyeom (sweet & spicy) and Megan Burger (spicy soy). The menu also features bao, chicken katsu curry, cro-waffles, and rice bowls, making it a solid stop for a calorie-rich refuel after a coastal ride.

bike_parking_detail: 4 racks within 100m: rack (6 spaces) at 8m; staple (4 spaces) at 23m; staple (4 spaces) at 49m; rack at 76m. Total: 14 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fully corroborates the OSM record: address, phone, and name all match. The site confirms takeout/online ordering via an 'Order Now' button and an explicitly chicken-focused menu with no stated vegetarian alternatives, consistent with the OSM diet:vegetarian=no tag. No bike parking, washroom, water refill, or other cyclist-specific amenity information appears anywhere on the site or in OSM tags.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active, independently operated restaurant on a well-trafficked Cook Street Village cycling corridor with a confirmed working website and online ordering.
